title: a11y screenshot: crash-safe layered alpha restore guard
desc: Crash-safe restore of layered window alpha during a11y screenshot suppression -- prevents windows staying invisible after taskkill/AccessViolation/SIGKILL of the screenshot process
steps: PROBLEM SuppressBlockingWindows in ScreenshotCommand.cs sets WS_EX_LAYERED + alpha=0 on every window above the capture rect; expects RestoreBlockingWindows to restore at end. External kill bypasses finally -- window stays invisible.

FIX ScreenshotCommand.AlphaRecovery.cs adds AlphaRecord(hwnd,prevStyle,prevAlpha) which writes to %TEMP%/wkappbot-screenshot/alpha-pending-{pid}.jsonl BEFORE SetLayeredWindowAttributes(0,0,LWA_ALPHA).
HOOKS Console.CancelKeyPress + AppDomain.ProcessExit + AppDomain.UnhandledException registered on first AlphaRecord() call.
RECOVERY RecoverOrphanedAlpha() runs in Program.Dispatch.Run() at every wkappbot startup; scans alpha-pending-*.jsonl, restores files whose PID is dead.
INVARIANT persist BEFORE alpha=0; recovery is idempotent.
ENTRY POINTS AlphaRecord, AlphaClearPending, RecoverOrphanedAlpha in csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/Commands.Private/ScreenshotCommand.AlphaRecovery.cs

PROBLEM: SuppressBlockingWindows in csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/Commands.Private/ScreenshotCommand.cs sets WS_EX_LAYERED + alpha=0 on every window above the capture rect; RestoreBlockingWindows in the matching finally puts it back. External kill (taskkill /F, OS AccessViolation, SIGKILL) bypasses the finally so windows stay invisible at alpha=0 -- user has to admin-PowerShell SetLayeredWindowAttributes back to 255.

PERSIST: ScreenshotCommand.AlphaRecovery.cs (new file) provides AlphaRecord(hwnd,prevStyle,prevAlpha) -- appends one JSONL line {hwnd,prevStyle,prevAlpha} to %TEMP%/wkappbot-screenshot/alpha-pending-{pid}.jsonl. SuppressBlockingWindows MUST call AlphaRecord BEFORE SetLayeredWindowAttributes(0,0,LWA_ALPHA) -- a kill in that 1-call gap is the only race we cannot self-cover.

GRACEFUL HOOKS: First AlphaRecord() call also registers Console.CancelKeyPress + AppDomain.CurrentDomain.ProcessExit + AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException; each handler reads the per-PID pending file and restores. Covers Ctrl-C, normal exit, .NET unhandled exception.

STARTUP RECOVERY: Program.Dispatch.cs Run() calls RecoverOrphanedAlpha() once before dispatch. RecoverOrphanedAlpha enumerates %TEMP%/wkappbot-screenshot/alpha-pending-*.jsonl, parses PID from filename, skips if PID is alive (file owner still running), otherwise restores each recorded window and deletes the file. This is the SIGKILL/AccessViolation/power-loss safety net -- the next wkappbot invocation heals what the dead one left behind.

CLEAR ON SUCCESS: RestoreBlockingWindows tail calls AlphaClearPending() which deletes %TEMP%/wkappbot-screenshot/alpha-pending-{pid}.jsonl. A clean run leaves no residue. Recovery is idempotent (re-applying a saved alpha to an already-restored window is a no-op), so a redundant restore from both in-process AND startup-scan is harmless.

EVIDENCE: D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/.wkappbot/evidence-alpha-restore.ps1 verifies (1) AlphaRecord, RecoverOrphanedAlpha, AlphaClearPending defined; (2) AlphaRecord wired in Suppress; (3) AlphaClearPending wired in Restore; (4) RecoverOrphanedAlpha wired in Run; (5) all 3 exit hooks present; (6) built binary newer than source.
